passage: I only looked up because a dog barked. My phone had said the shortest route was left, so I went left, then left again, down a lane with no lights and a fence with barbed wire. The little blue dot kept moving, and I kept following it. It was late and the road ended at a locked gate beside a building site. My heart sank. There was nobody. I turned around and walked quickly back to the main road, where a chai stall was open, and asked the man where the station was. He pointed the other way. I still use the map, but now I glance up every few steps. Shalini

qa.q: What made Shalini look up from the phone?
What was Shalini feeling when the road ended at a locked gate?
qa.a: Shalini felt alarmed and alone, since the heart sank and there was nobody around.

qa.q: What did Shalini do after noticing the danger, and what would you add?
qa.a: Shalini turned back to the main road and asked a stall owner, and could add that checking the surroundings sooner would have avoided the dark lane.

qa.q: What might the chai stall owner have thought when Shalini asked the way?
qa.a: The stall owner probably saw a lost traveller who had trusted the phone too much, and simply pointed the right way.

grounding: Shows a young traveller following a map app onto an unlit lane and only then looking up at what is actually around.

passage: Dusk in an unfamiliar town, and Dhruv had his eyes on his phone. "It says forty metres, then right." I walked beside him, watching the road. The right turn was a narrow lane with no pavement and no lights, where trucks were reversing. I said, "Are you sure?" but he was still reading the screen. A horn blared behind us. I grabbed his sleeve and pulled him against the wall. He looked up, pale, for the first time in ten minutes. We stopped at a tea shop and asked the owner for the walking route. Dhruv laughed, but his voice was thin. I did not say I told you so. Neelam

qa.q: What was in the narrow lane where the phone told Dhruv to turn?
qa.a: The narrow lane had no pavement and no lights, and trucks were reversing there.

qa.q: What might Neelam be feeling as Neelam walks beside Dhruv and watches the road?
qa.a: Neelam is probably worried and alert, noticing the danger while Dhruv reads the screen, and then relieved after the horn.

qa.q: What did Neelam and Dhruv do after the horn that was wise?
qa.a: They stopped at a tea shop and asked the owner for the walking route, checking the app against a local person.

qa.q: How does Dhruv seem to feel after looking up, and what is unclear?
qa.a: Dhruv looks pale and laughs in a thin voice, which suggests shock, though Neelam can only guess what he feels inside.

grounding: Shows a young traveller trusting a navigation app blindly onto an unsafe road until a horn makes him look up, as seen by a companion.
